system_prompt: AH-WORKER You audit code in a workspace using the list_files and read_file tools. For each audit step, read the files, then return ONLY JSON: {"step": N, "files": ["name"], "defects": [{"file": "name", "line": N, "explanation": "one sentence"}]}. Report only defects you saw in the file content, with the exact line number.

tools.description: Read one workspace file. Lines are numbered.
tools.name: read_file

path.description: File name inside the workspace, e.g. inventory.py

tools.description: List the files in the audit workspace.
tools.name: list_files

parts.text:
Audit step 1: Enumerate all files in inventory-service workspace and generate comprehensive file listing
Use the list_files and read_file tools on the workspace. Report the files and the defects you found with file and line.

{"step": 1, "files": ["report.py", "README.md", "inventory.py"], "defects": [{"file": "inventory.py", "line": 8, "explanation": "Dividing by len(sales) raises ZeroDivisionError when the sales list is empty, and nothing guards against that case."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 21, "explanation": "The loop starts at index 1, so low_stock never checks the first item and misses it even when its stock is below the threshold."}, {"file": "report.py", "line": 5, "explanation": "The file is opened without a context manager and never closed, so the written summary may not be flushed to disk and the file handle leaks."}]}

Audit step 2: Audit for code quality defects: complexity, duplication, naming conventions, error handling
Use the list_files and read_file tools on the workspace. Report the files and the defects you found with file and line.

{"step": 2, "files": ["report.py", "README.md", "inventory.py"], "defects": [{"file": "inventory.py", "line": 8, "explanation": "There is no error handling for an empty sales list, so average_daily_sales and its caller reorder_quantity raise an unhandled ZeroDivisionError."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 6, "explanation": "The loop on lines 5-7 rebuilds the built-in sum() by hand, which adds needless code where sum(sales) would do."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 21, "explanation": "The loop walks indices with range() instead of iterating over items directly, and the off-by-one start index this allows skips the first item."}, {"file": "report.py", "line": 5, "explanation": "open() is called without a with-block or try/finally, so the file is never closed and an exception during writing leaves a partly written, unflushed file."}]}

Audit step 3: Audit for correctness and logic errors: control flow, null checks, state management
Use the list_files and read_file tools on the workspace. Report the files and the defects you found with file and line.

{"step": 3, "files": ["report.py", "README.md", "inventory.py"], "defects": [{"file": "inventory.py", "line": 21, "explanation": "range(1, len(items)) starts at index 1, so the first item is never checked and a low-stock first item is silently left unflagged."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 8, "explanation": "Nothing checks for an empty or None sales list before dividing, so an empty list raises ZeroDivisionError and None raises TypeError when the loop starts."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 16, "explanation": "Line 8 uses true division, so the reorder quantity returned here can be a fraction such as 2.5 units instead of being rounded up to a whole number, which under-orders stock."}, {"file": "report.py", "line": 8, "explanation": "The function returns the row count while the file opened on line 5 is still open and unflushed, so a caller that reads the file next may find it empty or incomplete."}]}

Audit step 4: Audit for security and resource issues: injection vulnerabilities, resource leaks, access control
Use the list_files and read_file tools on the workspace. Report the files and the defects you found with file and line.
